focus: Q3: compare persistent surface-order options and identify the cheapest supported policy.
noveltyJustification: Four findings add direct compiler, doctor, runtime and fixture evidence beyond the provisional tieBreak recommendation in iteration 5; one refines that recommendation.
keyQuestions: Q3: How should a user-added surface outrank sk-code-opencode (registry priority field, native or fallback flag, tieBreak derived at mint time, --surface-hint, other), and which option is cheapest at acceptable risk?
answeredQuestions: Q3: How should a user-added surface outrank sk-code-opencode (registry priority field, native or fallback flag, tieBreak derived at mint time, --surface-hint, other), and which option is cheapest at acceptable risk?
ruledOut: A per-surface priority or rank field: the current explicit tieBreak already expresses the required order.
A native/fallback flag: it adds a second ordering rule and does not order multiple user surfaces.
Mint-derived precedence: the compiler already consumes the authored tieBreak, while registry array order is not the precedence contract.
--surface-hint as repository policy: it only reorders matched surfaces for a call that supplies a hint.

label: The authored hub tieBreak is copied into the compiled routing model and used to sort equal-score modes, so it is the current persistent precedence mechanism.

Doctor requires tieBreak to be an exact permutation of registered modes and separately enforces workflow modes before surfaces; adding rank without replacing this contract would create two order authorities.
surfaceHint is applied after route evaluation and only reorders already matched surface targets, so it cannot define a persistent repository default.
Existing surface-hint tests and canary fixtures distinguish no-hint tieBreak order from per-call hint order and are the required regression surface for any precedence change.

Rank and native/fallback metadata are absent from the current mode contract and routing-model projection, so either proposal requires new compiler and doctor behavior that the existing tieBreak does not need.
